exact_section.heading: 5.2 Clinical Features/Symptoms/Investigation; 5.3 Modified Centor Criteria

exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis (Sore Throat)

exact_source_references.source_version: EBI statutory guidance; last reviewed September 2024

exact_section.heading: Summary and recommendation — recurrent episodes, documentation, and functional impact
exact_section.locator: official guidance Summary and Recommendation sections
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports documenting recurrent sore-throat episodes attributed by a clinician to acute tonsillitis, episode history, normal-function impact, work or school impact, and complications without applying an automatic procedural threshold.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: Academy of Medical Royal Colleges Evidence-Based Interventions programme
exact_source_references.source_version: EBI statutory guidance; last reviewed September 2024

exact_section.heading: Recommendation and exclusions — shared decision and separate pathways
exact_section.locator: official guidance Recommendation and exclusion list
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports recording a clinician-completed benefit-risk-alternative discussion and recognizing sleep-disordered breathing, suspected cancer, recurrent quinsy, emergency presentations, immune deficiency, and other specialist contexts without recommending surgery.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.7 — skin cancers
exact_section.evidence_summary: Lists suspicious pigmented-lesion features including size change, irregular shape or colour, diameter, inflammation, oozing and sensation change, plus dermoscopy and referral contexts for melanoma, squamous-cell carcinoma, and basal-cell carcinoma.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.14.6–1.15.2 — information and safety netting
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports documenting warning symptoms, when to return for re-evaluation, agreed review, and patient-initiated review if symptoms recur, persist, worsen, or cause concern.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.1.6 — lung and pleural cancer respiratory features
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of unexplained haemoptysis and age- and smoking-context combinations involving unexplained cough, fatigue, breathlessness, chest pain, weight loss, appetite loss, recurrent chest infection, clubbing, lymphadenopathy, or chest signs.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — oesophageal, stomach, and pancreatic cancer features
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of dysphagia, weight-loss combinations, and jaundice in recommendation-specific age and symptom contexts; it does not assert cancer or an automatic referral decision.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.5 — colorectal cancer features
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of rectal bleeding, change in bowel habit, abdominal pain, weight loss, anaemia, and rectal-mass contexts with recommendation-specific age qualifiers; it does not assert cancer.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.8.1–1.8.5 — laryngeal, oral, and thyroid cancer recognition features
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of recommendation-qualified persistent unexplained hoarseness, unexplained or persistent neck lump, oral ulceration lasting more than 3 weeks, lip or oral-cavity lump, red or red-and-white oral patch, and unexplained thyroid lump. It does not assert cancer or generate referral.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.4.1–1.4.3 — breast cancer recognition and referral
exact_section.locator: recommendations organised by site, breast cancer section
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of an unexplained breast lump and age-qualified nipple or skin changes for referral consideration; it does not assert cancer or generate a referral decision.

exact_section.heading: 1. Background

exact_source_references.source_organisation: Dubai Health Authority
exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis (Sore Throat)

exact_section.heading: 2. Scope; 3. Purpose; 4. Applicability
exact_section.evidence_summary: Defines Dubai telehealth scope and exclusions for emergency and controlled-medication prescribing.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: Dubai Health Authority
exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis (Sore Throat)

exact_section.heading: 5.2 Clinical Features/Symptoms/Investigation; 5.3 Modified Centor Criteria
exact_section.evidence_summary: Lists swallowing pain, fever, cough and URTI features, tonsillar findings, cervical nodes, rash, and clinician-selected GAS testing context.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: Dubai Health Authority
exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis (Sore Throat)

exact_section.heading: 7. Management; 7.5 Follow-up
exact_section.evidence_summary: Covers clinician-led symptom care, communication, treatment decisions, reassessment, and follow-up without authorising autonomous medication output.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: Dubai Health Authority
exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis (Sore Throat)

exact_section.heading: 8. Referral Criteria and Red Flags
exact_section.evidence_summary: Lists airway, swallowing, breathing, pain, immune compromise, neck stiffness, dehydration, and complication prompts for escalation.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: Dubai Health Authority
exact_source_references.source_document_title: DHA Telehealth Clinical Guidelines for Virtual Management of Acute Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis (Sore Throat)

exact_section.heading: Executive Summary and clinical course
exact_section.evidence_summary: States the adult and paediatric scope and expected recovery or reassessment context for viral and GAS pharyngitis.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: Academy of Medical Royal Colleges Evidence-Based Interventions programme
exact_source_references.source_version: EBI statutory guidance; last reviewed September 2024

exact_section.heading: Summary and recommendation — recurrent episodes, documentation, and functional impact
exact_section.locator: official guidance Summary and Recommendation sections
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports documenting recurrent sore-throat episodes attributed by a clinician to acute tonsillitis, episode history, normal-function impact, work or school impact, and complications without applying an automatic procedural threshold.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: Academy of Medical Royal Colleges Evidence-Based Interventions programme
exact_source_references.source_version: EBI statutory guidance; last reviewed September 2024

exact_section.heading: Recommendation and exclusions — shared decision and separate pathways
exact_section.locator: official guidance Recommendation and exclusion list
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports recording a clinician-completed benefit-risk-alternative discussion and recognizing sleep-disordered breathing, suspected cancer, recurrent quinsy, emergency presentations, immune deficiency, and other specialist contexts without recommending surgery.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.7.1–1.7.7 — skin cancers
exact_section.evidence_summary: Lists suspicious pigmented-lesion features including size change, irregular shape or colour, diameter, inflammation, oozing and sensation change, plus dermoscopy and referral contexts for melanoma, squamous-cell carcinoma, and basal-cell carcinoma.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.14.6–1.15.2 — information and safety netting
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports documenting warning symptoms, when to return for re-evaluation, agreed review, and patient-initiated review if symptoms recur, persist, worsen, or cause concern.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.1.1–1.1.6 — lung and pleural cancer respiratory features
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of unexplained haemoptysis and age- and smoking-context combinations involving unexplained cough, fatigue, breathlessness, chest pain, weight loss, appetite loss, recurrent chest infection, clubbing, lymphadenopathy, or chest signs.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.7 — oesophageal, stomach, and pancreatic cancer features
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of dysphagia, weight-loss combinations, and jaundice in recommendation-specific age and symptom contexts; it does not assert cancer or an automatic referral decision.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.5 — colorectal cancer features
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of rectal bleeding, change in bowel habit, abdominal pain, weight loss, anaemia, and rectal-mass contexts with recommendation-specific age qualifiers; it does not assert cancer.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.8.1–1.8.5 — laryngeal, oral, and thyroid cancer recognition features
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of recommendation-qualified persistent unexplained hoarseness, unexplained or persistent neck lump, oral ulceration lasting more than 3 weeks, lip or oral-cavity lump, red or red-and-white oral patch, and unexplained thyroid lump. It does not assert cancer or generate referral.

exact_source_references.source_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence

exact_section.heading: Recommendations 1.4.1–1.4.3 — breast cancer recognition and referral
exact_section.locator: recommendations organised by site, breast cancer section
exact_section.evidence_summary: Supports clinician recognition of an unexplained breast lump and age-qualified nipple or skin changes for referral consideration; it does not assert cancer or generate a referral decision.
